claims.claim: Cyril of Alexandria was the Patriarch (bishop) of Alexandria, Egypt, serving from 412 until his death in 444, and was born around 376.
He was a leading 5th‑century theologian whose extensive biblical commentaries form a major part of his literary output.

Passages from the Matthew fragments, such as a quotation of Matthew 27:25, have been cited in modern discussions of anti‑Jewish polemics and have sparked controversy over their omission in translations.
